questions.prompt: Which statement about DNA structure is FALSE?

options.text: Adenine pairs with thymine and guanine pairs with cytosine.
DNA has a roughly constant width of about 2 nm.
DNA is double-stranded and twists into a double helix.
The sugar-phosphate backbone is held together by hydrogen bonds.

questions.explanation: False. The backbone is held together by strong covalent bonds; hydrogen bonds hold the two strands together across the middle.

questions.prompt: In Griffith's experiment, which injection killed the mouse even though neither component killed a mouse on its own?

options.text: Heat-killed smooth cells + live rough cells

questions.explanation: Heat-killed S + live R killed the mouse and living S cells were recovered — the R cells had been transformed.

questions.prompt: Avery added DNase to the heat-killed S + live R mixture and the mouse lived. What did this show?

options.text: The capsule is made of DNA

questions.explanation: Destroying DNA blocked transformation, while destroying protein (protease) did not — so DNA is the genetic material.

questions.prompt: What did Rosalind Franklin contribute to the discovery of DNA's structure, and why didn't she share the Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Using X-ray crystallography, she crystallized DNA and produced Photo 51, showing DNA is a double helix. She died at 38 (likely from X-ray exposure) and the Nobel Prize (1962) is not awarded posthumously.

questions.prompt: Which component of a nucleotide makes it unique (A vs G vs C vs T)?
questions.explanation: The nitrogenous base is the only part that differs among nucleotides.

questions.prompt: A bacterial genome is 30% thymine. What percentage is guanine?
Which statement comparing DNA and RNA is FALSE?

options.text: DNA uses deoxyribose; RNA uses ribose.
RNA contains uracil in place of thymine.

questions.explanation: False. Uracil pairs with adenine, just as thymine does.

questions.prompt: Which end of a DNA strand begins with a phosphate group attached to the sugar?
questions.explanation: The 5' end starts with a phosphate on carbon 5; the 3' end finishes with an –OH on carbon 3.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme unzips and unwinds the double helix to create a replication fork?
questions.explanation: Helicase unzips the helix. Gyrase uncoils supercoiling first; primase lays primers; ligase joins fragments.

questions.prompt: Why is the lagging strand built in Okazaki fragments?

options.text: Ligase destroys the strand as it is built
Helicase can only open short sections at a time
The lagging strand is made of RNA
DNA polymerase and primase can only synthesize 5' to 3', which runs away from the fork on that strand

questions.explanation: Because synthesis is restricted to 5'→3', one template strand must be copied backward in short primed pieces that ligase later joins.

questions.prompt: List the five replication enzymes in the order they act and give each one's job.
questions.explanation: Gyrase — uncoils supercoiled DNA; Helicase — unzips/unwinds the helix forming the fork; Primase — lays an RNA primer; DNA polymerase — adds complementary nucleotides 5'→3' and replaces the primer with DNA; Ligase — joins Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand.

questions.prompt: How many replication forks form when a bacterium replicates its circular chromosome?
questions.explanation: Two helicases leave the origin in opposite directions, creating two forks that meet on the other side of the loop.

questions.prompt: Ciprofloxacin stops bacterial growth by targeting which step?

options.text: Adding nucleotides to the new strand

questions.explanation: Cipro inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase, so DNA can't be uncoiled and replicated.

questions.prompt: Which statement about genotype and phenotype is FALSE?

options.text: Genotype refers to the genes and nucleotide sequences in the genome.
A gene encodes the primary structure of a protein.
Being Gram-negative is a phenotypic trait.
Being a facultative anaerobe is a phenotypic trait.

questions.explanation: False. Genotype determines phenotype, not the other way around.

questions.prompt: What did Craig Venter accomplish with Mycoplasma genitalium?

options.text: Created the first artificial genome and got a cell to run on it
Built the first recombinant DNA molecule

questions.explanation: He sequenced its 521-gene chromosome, synthesized an artificial copy, and transplanted it into a chromosome-less cell.

questions.prompt: Which DNA strand runs 5'→3' and has the same sequence as the mRNA? (slides)
questions.explanation: The coding strand matches the mRNA (T instead of U); the 3'→5' non-coding strand is the template.

questions.prompt: What does 'semi-conservative' mean, and why does replication take most of a bacterium's ~30-minute generation time?
questions.explanation: Each new double helix keeps one original (parent) strand and pairs it with one newly built (daughter) strand. Copying the whole chromosome is the slow step; the actual splitting in binary fission happens quickly.

questions.prompt: How did Hershey and Chase confirm DNA is the genetic material? (slides/textbook)
questions.explanation: They labeled T2 phage protein with ³⁵S and phage DNA with ³²P, let each infect E. coli, then blended and centrifuged. Only the ³²P (DNA) ended up inside the bacteria, so the phage's DNA — not its protein — directs new phage production.
